correctness.rationale: Derivative identity is obtained by integration by parts with vanishing boundaries; strictly increasing OU hazard has exactly one sign change, and the ratio of positive/negative Laplace contributions decreases strictly to zero. This proves exactly one or zero stationary minima of reciprocal response, including boundary equality. Monotone likelihood ratio in correlation time proves moment ratio strictly decreases, and dominated Gaussian scaling gives both endpoints. Scaled derivative has one limiting positive zero and explicit bracket convergence. 908 independently computed finite SciPy checks passed; finite checks are not the proof.

value.rationale: The question arises directly from a model reporting a finite optimal spin-flip rate for a few memory choices. Classifying the complete phase diagram identifies a nontrivial regime where increasing OU memory extinguishes the optimum, with a uniquely defined critical memory time and a physical example (tau_c about 4.22146). The sharp 1/tau blow-up of optimal switching resolves the singular white-noise boundary. These all-parameter structural conclusions inform timescale selection and cannot be inferred from a few numerical optima or a sufficient existence condition.
